question.text: A fund with a 'hard cap' on corpus means:

answer.text: The fund can raise capital without any limit
The maximum corpus cannot be exceeded under any circumstances
The fund can only invest in hardware companies
The fund must invest a minimum amount in each deal

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the workbook, a hard cap is a maximum cap on the fund's corpus that cannot be breached. A soft cap, by contrast, is a target amount that can be extended as required. The Trap: Both the hard cap and the soft cap (including any green-shoe option) along with fund terms are required to be disclosed in the PPM, but only the hard cap is absolute; the soft cap is flexible. Note: The distinction between hard cap and soft cap is part of the corpus and fund-terms disclosures investors review when evaluating an AIF.
